key_insight: Keeping ReLU firing rates within a target range helps prevent inactive and always-on neurons, sustaining plasticity during continual learning.
engineering_relevance: This approach may help engineering models adapt to changing data, though the abstract reports no solid-mechanics validation.
method: Measure each ReLU neuron's firing rate as the fraction of positive pre-activations.
Adjust per-neuron thresholds to keep firing rates within a target range.
Balance neuron activity without periodically reinitializing learned units.
evidence_signal: Load balancing matches or exceeds reset-based methods on continual ImageNet and class-incremental CIFAR-100, and improves Rainbow DQN on Atari over a LayerNorm baseline.
watch_item: Target firing-rate ranges and threshold-update settings require implementation choices whose sensitivity is not specified in the abstract.
paper_title: Load Balancing Neurons: Firing-Rate Control Sustains Plasticity in Continual Learning
